BMR Calculator

Basal Metabolic Rate

Step 1 of 4

What is BMR?

Your Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) is the number of calories your body burns while completely at rest — just to keep your heart beating, lungs breathing, and organs functioning. It is the minimum energy your body needs to survive.

The formula used (Mifflin-St Jeor)

Men: BMR = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) − (5 × age) + 5

Women: BMR = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) − (5 × age) − 161

This is the most accurate BMR formula validated by clinical research for the general population.

How to use your BMR

BMR on its own only tells you what you burn doing nothing. To find the calories you actually need each day, you must factor in your activity level — that is your TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure). Your BMR is the foundation of your TDEE calculation.

BMR vs TDEE — what is the difference?

  • BMR = calories burned at complete rest (no movement at all)
  • TDEE = BMR × activity multiplier (accounts for your daily movement and exercise)

Always use TDEE for calorie planning, not BMR alone.
